CG_WorldPosToScreenPos(int localClientNum, refdefView*, const float world[3],
                       float outScreenXY[2]) -> char

IDA types arg2 as int, but it is the CG_GetRefdefView pointer: the call site
does `a2 + 32` and hands it to a float* (the viewport width/height pair at
+32/+36).

RETURN: only AL is defined -- it tail-returns CG_ProjectViewDirToScreenPos's
`char`. 1 = in front of the camera, 0 = behind, in which case outScreenXY
still receives CLAMPED EDGE coordinates, so the return value is the only way
to tell. Declaring the return wider reads register residue (see CLAUDE.md
RULE A17).

OUTPUT SPACE: refdef VIEWPORT pixels (the +32/+36 pair). LUI_WorldToScreenPosition
normalises by GetRenderTargetDimensions' g_renderTargetWidth/Height, which are
the same two globals InternalConsole uses as its draw-space window size -- so
in the ordinary fullscreen case the output is directly usable as
R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic / R_AddCmdDrawText pixel coordinates.

It calls CG_GetLocalClientGlobals internally, but from INSIDE the image, so
the Arxan retaddr check that forbids the mod calling that function directly
does not apply to calling this one.

CL_Demo_InterpolateCameraPose -- descriptive name, BEHAVIOUR-PROVEN (no MW3
twin exists; checked 2026-08-11).

The engine's own camera interpolator, used on the NATIVE demo playback branch
of CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove. Lerps a stored pose pair into the freecam fields:

  frac = cg[498397]                       (byte 1993588)
  playbackData + 5439296 .. +5439316      TARGET pose (origin xyz, angles xyz)
  playbackData + 5439324 .. +5439344      PREVIOUS pose
  playbackData + 5439348  byte            snap flag: prev := target, then clear

  cg[588912..914] = prev + (target - prev) * frac                (origin)
  cg[588915..917] = prev + normalize180(target - prev) * frac    (angles)

The angle path uses the *0.0027777778 (1/360) then x-(x+0.5) then *360 trick,
which is AngleNormalize180 -- i.e. the engine already does shortest-arc angle
interpolation here.

NOTE FOR ANY DOLLY/CAMERA WORK: feeding the target/prev pair would be the
elegant way to drive a camera, but NOTHING has established who writes that
pair or when, so per the doctrine it must not be written. Overwriting the
RESULT (the cg fields above) after this returns is the safe equivalent.
